newsitem.title: New Zealand: CRICKET-ENGLAND ON FORM AS FIRST NZ TEST NEARS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND ON FORM AS FIRST NZ TEST NEARS.

text.p: England's smooth progress towards this week's first cricket test against New Zealand continued unimpeded on Monday when they beat Northern Districts by 10 wickets with more than four sessions to spare.

Northern Districts, who began the third day of the four-day match day on 99 for one, were dismissed for 259, leaving England 35 to win, which openers Nick Knight and captain Mike Atherton got in 8.1 overs.
That gives England two first-class wins well inside the distance since their arrival in New Zealand, and Atherton admitted his pre-test plans for the team had worked out ideally.
"I'm delighted with the way we've started the New Zealand tour," he said.
"...We've controlled them throughout, played good cricket and haven't really had a bad session."

Another piece in England's test puzzle fell into place in the first hour on Monday when fast-medium bowler Darren Gough removed overnight batsmen Blair Pocock and Matthew Bell in an excellent seven-over spell.
Gough bowled Bell with the fourth ball of the day, without the batsman adding to his overnight 35.
He then had Pocock leg before wicket, playing across the line, for 69.
Alan Mullally warmed up for the first test with a useful return of four for 52, Gough finished with three for 51 and Craig White took two for 61.
England will travel to Auckland on Tuesday morning and have two days training before the first test starts on Friday.
